question.problem:
Consider the following system of differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)
$$

Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t),$ where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and $u(t)$ is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for ${x}_{p}(t)$ is given below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t)$

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${x}_{p}^{′}(t)=Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)$

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)$

$\text{L6}:\,$ ${u}^{′}(t)={Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)$

$\text{L7}:\,$ $u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L3}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L2}$ into the {{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L6}$ follows from line $\text{L5}$ by {{field-2}} both sides of the equation.

$\,$ Line $\text{L7}$ follows from line $\text{L6}$ by {{field-3}} both sides of the equation.

$\,$ Line $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L7}$ into {{field-4}} .

choices.value: solution of the system of ODEs

current_example.problem:
Consider the following system of differential equations:

$$
\mathbf{x}'(t) =
A
\mathbf{x}(t) +
\mathbf{f}(t)
$$

Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form $\mathbf{x}_p(t)  = \Phi \mathbf{u}(t),$ where $\Phi$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and $\mathbf{u}(t)$ is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for $\mathbf x_p(t)$ is given below. 

$\textrm{L1}{:}\:$ $\mathbf{x}_p(t)  = \Phi \mathbf{u}(t)$

$\textrm{L2}{:}\:$ $\mathbf{x}'_p(t) = \Phi \mathbf{u}'(t) + \Phi' \mathbf{u}(t)$

$\textrm{L3}{:}\:$ $\Phi \mathbf{u}'(t) + \Phi' \mathbf{u}(t) = A \Phi \mathbf{u}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t)$

$\textrm{L4}{:}\:$ $\Phi' = A \Phi$

$\textrm{L5}{:}\:$ $\Phi \mathbf{u}'(t) = \mathbf{f}(t)$

$\textrm{L6}{:}\:$ $\mathbf{u}'(t) = \Phi^{-1}(t) \mathbf{f}(t)$

$\textrm{L7}{:}\:$ $\displaystyle\mathbf{u}(t) = \int \Phi^{-1} \mathbf{f}(t) \, \text{d}t$

$\textrm{L8}{:}\:$ $\displaystyle\mathbf{x}_p(t) = \Phi \int \Phi^{-1}\mathbf{f}(t) \, \text{d}t$

Fill in the blanks with the correct reasons to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\quad$ Line $\textrm{L6}$ follows from line $\textrm{L5}$ by  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14159277/assets/037fcabc9d8cef762d7c5808842d49fa77d77919421aebc7e69a9f790d623419.svg) both sides of the equation.

$\quad$ Line $\textrm{L8}$ is obtained by substituting $\textrm{L7}$ into ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14159277/assets/df5cafa590bef72aea23a19b457a7cf4301f2eba2c734789b06be7bf57dafe55.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's examine each statement in turn.

- We first consider line $\textrm{L4}.$ Since $\Phi$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system $\mathbf{x}'(t) =A\mathbf{x}(t),$ i.e., by substituting any column $\mathbf{c}(t)$ of $\Phi$ into the homogeneous system, we get

$$
\mathbf{c}'(t) =A\mathbf{c}(t),
$$

where $\mathbf{c}'(t)$ is the corresponding column of derivatives in $\Phi.$ As a result, this means that $\Phi' = A \Phi.$ Therefore, $\textrm{L4}$ follows from the fact that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14159277/assets/557b30e22674ef3931a150dc9c6afcabfdf32763868766a5dca2208bf3631f10.svg) matrix.

- Next, we consider lines $\textrm{L5}$ and $\textrm{L6}.$ Since $\Phi$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are linearly independent. So, $\Phi$ is invertible. Therefore, $\textrm{L6}$ follows from $\textrm{L5}$ by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14159277/assets/ec0da6dd788e79929e09e184d699497658b2a2b9010f7f04455f51c0856da5f9.svg) both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\cdot Φ{u}^{′}(t) & ={Φ}^{-1}\cdot f(t) \\ ({Φ}^{-1}Φ)\cdot {u}^{′}(t) & ={Φ}^{-1}\cdot f(t) \\ {u}^{′}(t) & ={Φ}^{-1}\cdot f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

- Finally, we consider lines $\textrm{L1},$ $\textrm{L7},$ and $\textrm{L8}.$ Substituting

$$
\mathbf{u}(t) = \int \Phi^{-1} \mathbf{f}(t) \, \text{d}t
$$

from $\textrm{L7}$ into $\textrm{L1},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φu(t) \\  & =Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\textrm{L8}$ is obtained by substituting $\textrm{L7}$ into  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14159277/assets/3384bd1209b3ca46ac7edcf2aaea4b18248fcb8cc6dae86288dfb4890049c199.svg)
